reviews.author: Ana M.
reviews.text:
I have lived here long enough to confidently say that there are serious systemic service issues that need to be addressed.

The valet trash service, which residents are charged $25 per month for, has been inconsistent since November. Entire buildings are regularly missed, trash sits outside doors for extended periods, and residents are still charged for the service regardless of performance. I was informed my unit was placed on a “tracking system” to prevent further misses, yet my building is being missed again.

Parking enforcement is another ongoing issue. Vehicles frequently park on the curb despite open spaces being available, creating unsafe conditions when pulling out of parking spots.

That said, I do want to specifically acknowledge David in the office. He has consistently gone above and beyond when issues arise. On multiple occasions, he has personally resolved issues including collecting my trash when service was missed and even handled maintenance-related follow-ups when vendors did not show up. He is responsive, professional, and clearly cares about residents.

The issue here is not individual staff effort — it is a lack of consistent management oversight and vendor accountability. A large community should have systems in place that prevent recurring failures, not rely on individual employees to manually correct them.

I truly hope leadership takes these concerns seriously and evaluates vendor performance, enforcement practices, and communication processes. Residents deserve to receive the services they are paying for. It would also be extremely helpful to get the actual manager on the phone or consistent email follow up from her.

Update (June 2026):

I am updating my original review because, unfortunately, very little has changed.

The concerns I raised previously regarding communication, accountability, and management responsiveness remain unresolved. The property manager is still virtually impossible to reach. Phone calls go unanswered, emails often receive delayed responses or no response at all, and obtaining direct communication from management continues to be an ongoing challenge.

Residents were informed that the pool would reopen by Memorial Day weekend. It is now June 13, and the pool remains closed with little to no proactive communication regarding delays, timelines, or expectations. Amenities are a significant factor in choosing and paying for an apartment community, and residents deserve transparency when those amenities are unavailable for extended periods.

Parking enforcement issues continue, valet trash service remains inconsistent, and many concerns seem to require repeated follow-up before any action is taken. While individual office staff members continue to do what they can, residents should not have to rely on specific employees stepping in to compensate for larger operational and management failures.

My original review acknowledged that the problem was not individual staff effort but rather a lack of management oversight and accountability. Unfortunately, after several more months, that assessment remains accurate.

At this point, what residents need is not another apology or assurance that improvements are being made. We need consistent communication, accessible management, enforcement of community policies, functioning amenities, and delivery of the services we are paying for.
reviews.response: We apologize for the issues you have experienced with valet trash and parking enforcement. We understand your frustration and are actively working to improve these services. We appreciate your kind words for David and will address the vendor accountability issues. Your feedback is valued and we will continue to strive for excellence in all areas. Thank you for bringing these concerns to our attention.

reviews.author: Nah F.
reviews.text: This is a BUYER BEWARE! My experience with this complex and property management group has been displeasing. First and foremost, my apartment is infested with roaches. The building is infested with roaches, I discovered this when my neighbor opened their patio doors shortly after opening mine as this issue has a stench to it. The reviews are true. I wish I had used them to make my decision. The floors are poorly done so they're porous which causes very humid conditions when attempting to mediate such an issue. My bathtub has cracks in the paint which has been used to seal over the tiling. Therefore, every time I shower I become severely itchy in the process, which lets me know there is a violent mold growth underneath it. It doesn't matter how much I clean, it comes right back. The overflow drain in both bathroom sinks are rusted over and smell bad. The water sometimes smells of sulfur, which is a sign of bacteria. Furthermore, my apartment was filthy. Unbeknownst to the naked eye, but once I began cleaning, it was evident that my apartment was not at all sanitized from previous residents. There is pet hair EVERYWHERE. Mind you, I do NOT own one. Even after their vendor came by with an industrial floor polisher to clean the carpets, pet hair was still in the carpet, that lets you know just how much there was. There was outside debris in the carpet, fingernails of all types (press on, acrylic, and natural), dead roaches, and other things like screws. Oddly the floors took almost two weeks to dry. Which let me know that the flooring was poorly done. The washer and dryer were also disgusting. They are riddled with pet hair. The dryer hose had crunchy roaches in it. Even the dishwasher had some very disgusting gunk in the filter. The care to have my apartment made ready was almost non existent. My move-in date had even been pushed back THREE times. The first time because the apartment I applied for wouldn't be ready by my move-in date. Second, at my request to accommodate this move from out of state. Third, for their accounting close out period. There was plenty of time to make sure that my apartment would be healthy and sanitized. I wasn't even given a move-in inspection form because it needed to be "updated." I am truly disappointed. Now, these are most of my complaints. Property management's solution took some time to even begin, as I was patient and understanding of those who were affected by the hurricane. They have done their part to send pest control on multiple occasions to service my apartment and then finally to service the building. They agreed to a transfer request, however, the options were terrible. The first smelled like animal urine and cigarettes and was extremely humid. The second was also extremely humid, meaning the thermostat was set at 71 and it was HOT and muggy in the apartment. The next few had signs that they were also roach infested. Another smelled like mold. The only apartment I liked was because it had been totally renovated, the floors had been done properly and the work looked as though it was done by quality vendors. My issue now is that I am being charged for a washer and dryer that I could not use due to their filthiness and an apartment that I couldn't even unpack due to all of the issues. Dealing with these issues have been costly for me. I shouldn't have to pay for the month that I had to complain repeatedly before getting a true resolution. Mind you, it took a few days short of a month. Not to mention, I will have to incur moving expenses AGAIN. Paying for movers, renting a truck, time off of work. These things add up, fast. reviews.author: Aubrey T.
reviews.text:
This is probably the cheapest place to stay in chamblee and there’s a reason why. When we began filling out papers for this place, everything was fine. We paid the deposits and required fees. We had a pet fee as we were bringing a couple of cats, but nothing crazy. We didn’t receive our welcome letter until 3 days before we move in, so I had 3 days to set up all utilities. While this wasn’t preferable, I managed to get it done. Only to find out 1 day before our move in date that the lady in the office gave us a welcome letter with the WRONG UNIT NUMBER. So everything that I had gotten set up (gas, electric, insurance) had to be redone. That was red flag number one.
During our stay, we had a few repair requests that didn’t get handled for months on end. A big one was the oven that didn’t turn on that we submitted multiple requests for that never got fixed. There was a big project at one point to upgrade all of the toilets. It looked like they had ripped out the old toilet from the wall just to install a new one and not fix any holes. Don’t even get me started on the landlord special bathtub. The entire bathtub, tile and all, had been painted with white paint. Not something that affected my day-to-day, but I expected more for the amount of rent we paid.
I left everything as is and was initially not going to leave a review as the rest of our stay seemed to go on without being bothered too much… until it was time for deposit refunds.
My sister and I were renting a unit and our lease was up 6/30/2023. I primarily stayed with my boyfriend but would occasionally stay at Chatsworth. I paid my half of the rent, but my room remained vacant aside from some clothes and small furniture. My sister signed a lease and moved out 5/24/2023, over a month before our lease was up. We fulfilled our contractual obligations and paid through the rest of the lease without any issue. The apartment had been vacant since 5/24/2023. As my sister moved out and I moved in with my boyfriend.
It’s now 8/7 and we receive a check for only half of our deposit. When I questioned the property management email (not 100% sure who I was speaking with but I have a good idea), I was informed that they took half of our deposit due to a “flea infestation”. Keep in mind, we paid a pet-fee was was non refundable, so this “flea treatment” should have been paid for through the pet fee. There was no itemization sent with the check.
When I told them that there was no way the pets could have fleas as we maintained frequent vet visits AND the apartment had been vacant for over a month (it’s not likely that fleas can survive longer than 2 weeks without a host), she told me that we did NOT move out in May, but we moved out on 6/30, like our lease says. Believe me, if I could have managed to secure a place at the same time my lease ended, I wouldn’t have had to break my bank paying first and last months rent AND a deposit on a new place while still having to pay the last months rent on this apartment.
I’ve offered to prove our move out date with Uhaul rentals, newly signed leases, and I’ve offered to prove the pets were flea free by providing vet bills and statements. They just want to keep half of our deposit, so they don’t want to see any of it.
When I asked for proof of the flea fumigation, she sent me some rinky-dink form without any dates or signatures and expected me to take it at face value. She claimed it was an internal fumigation and that “there are plenty of witnesses”. Of course there was, they all work for you?? Additionally, in the email, she insinuated that we were lucky that’s all we got charged for as there was a “pet smell” that they didn’t charge us for.
Keep in mind, we had a first floor apartment. They are very dark, damp, and retain smells like no other. My assumption was that the repair/cleaning crew came in AFTER 6/30 and may have caught a smell of cat litter and assumed our pets had fleas, even though there couldn’t have possibly been any evidence.
I’m eating this half of the deposit to share my experience and warn others to BEWARE!!!

reviews.author: Steven K.
reviews.text:
Thankfully, my family is in our last week here!
This complex has become a blight to the city of Chamblee.
In 2017 when I moved in, this used to be an older complex that had a few quirks that were quickly addressed.
Now, after several maintenance & leasing companies disregarding the needs of the residents and property for the last 3-4 years, this property has become a slum. Silver Pointe Management has done everything to show that they do not care for the property.
Landscaping company used to come weekly. Fall cleanup is now non-existent. Now, an understaffed and under equipped landscape company come with blowers and pile the leaves against the buildings and under bushes. Fallen limbs left behind. This issue exacerbates the next problem...
Pests. You name it, this place has them. Roaches, palmetto bugs, rats. The entire property is infested. I've shown the leasing office videos of living roaches in our light fixtures. Rats roaming the property nowhere near the dumpster. I advised them 3 weeks ago that the problem was so bad with the roaches, I've woken up with them IN MY BED! After calling them about this problem, they promised pest service every week for the remainder of our stay.
They haven't serviced our apartment one time in 3 weeks. Still killing roaches in the apartment.
Trash pickup. If you don't find your trash left at the front door instead of being picked up, you'll probably find it left on a curb the next day. Trash is constantly left behind.
The dumpster. It's right by the main entrance. Constantly overflowing. Constantly broken. An embarrassment to drive by. Invite guests? No way. How would you want to show anyone where you live when that is the 1st thing you see at the entrance?
The smell in the summertime is overwhelming! Never cleaned, always broke.
Oh, the entrance. You get to drive past a mangled gate knocked off the rack. Unrepaired in over a year. Transients have begun parking overnight in the complex.
Maintenance. Yeah, right... what maintenance. Tickets go unanswered. If and when they do show up, they don't even know what for. Show up with the wrong ticket. Dirty lots, broken or malfunctioning flood lights. Large swaths of the parking lot are dark at night.
The gym smells and is constantly left unclean. No sanitizer or paper towels.
The pool has been closed more this summer than available to the residents. My apartment faces the rear pool. It was green most of the summer.
Do yourself a favor, walk away! Don't come here! Save yourself the stress! You'll be forgotten here, until you don't pay the rent on time.

When reaching out to the corporate office directly, they are completely unresponsive and have ignored the 6 emails I have sent. Additionally, phone calls are automatically directed to voicemail no matter which prompt is selected through the corporate number. Each time I have spoken with or emailed the property manager, Thanra Alvarado, I have been met with what I can only describe as disdain and condescension. Even the leasing, Sonya, has hung up on my roommate when reporting service request over the phone multiple times and, when addressed, said there was no point in further conversation. Whether service requests are submitted online, in person, over the phone, or via email we are always told they will be addressed only to find out that they were forgotten or marked as complete when they have not been.

The management seems to be trying to renovate apartments and scrape by until they can sell to the next company without investing anything in the residents living here.

The pest issue is one of the largest prevailing issues and has been met with complete incompetence. We were told that our building had a GERMAN COCKROACH INFESTATION by the service team and immediately submitted a request for pest control in the portal. When calling the office we were told that THEY FORGOT and the next few times that pest control CAME TOO LATE TO SERVICE our apartment. All of this accompanied by our window being broken and not repaired from 8/21 to 9/24. Completely unacceptable.

I had hoped this apartment would be a home but has ended up being an incredibly disappointing and disgusting place to live. There are no excuses at this point for the conditions of this community. Yet, excuses are all that management will give you. When reporting this and giving notice, I was told sorry and that I would be charged termination fees and the full notice to move and have not received a response to emails since.

I just moved out from this complex but I would have continued living here at least one more year.

Pros: the neighborhood, so quiet, nice, nearby major highways, shopping centers, restaurants, and beautiful parks.
It was a very quiet complex, working or studying from home was delightful.
Nice grounds, maintenance did what was possible to keep grounds pretty nice and groomed.
Very spacious apartments ( I had 1b/1b) and the place was pretty spacious.
Maintenance was always courteous and fixed  my issues.
Plenty of parking spaces around my unit.

The gym was great, plenty of free weights. I loved using it. (It is kind of small and sometimes people leave things messed out or break things but that happens everywhere)

Cons: they are older units so my apartment very often needed some sort of maintenance, sometimes the leasing office would dispatch them right away other times you would have to be more insistent, but I always had someone helping me, some issues would be fixed right away while other would take more time.

Some neighbors were very inconsiderate, no picking after their pets. And since I was on the ground floor I had to deal with this a lot.

There is only one big trash dumpster at the entrance, it can be annoying to take the trash out there and many people just decided to accumulate trash on their units or breezeways, luckily my unit was pretty good at keeping things neat.

Sometimes you had to be a bit insistent with maintenance issues, but Elizabeth and Ebonnae were always helpful to me.

I was on the ground floor so I had ants and spiders but pest control always helped when I requested.

Overall it is a good place, I guess having good neighbors help a lot to have a good experience. Good value and great location.

reviews.author: Isaam B.
reviews.text:
If I could give this place 0 stars I would. I can NOT wait until next month when our lease is up!!! My husband and I have been here for 2years now. We should of left last year but we really didn't want to move again so soon. Oh how we regret that decision.

So now I am going to start from the beginning. Bare with me because this is long! From the start I knew something was up with this complex but my husband wanted to give it a chance. When we first came to visit this place, they showed us a VERY NICE model apartment. I was very spacious with nice sized walk in closets, a sunroom and a balcony. Once the tour was over, we told the lady we were going to think on it and possibly be back. We decided that we liked the place and went back to talk to the staff member again. We asked if those specific amenities would be in the apartment that she said was available for us and she said yes. Oh yeah, I don't want to leave out that we were told our apartment was going to be on the first floor. Which was good because that's what we wanted.
We didn't see our actual apartment until the day of move in because we were coming from Columbus Ga. ANd the back and forth with apartment searching was a bit much for us. We had no reason to think that the staff member was lying about anything because we never had such crazy problems with our other three apartments (We moved so much due to the military).
The day we moved in, we found out our apartment was on THE SECOND FREAKING FLOOR, THERE WERE NO WALK IN CLOSETS, AND NO BALCONY!!!! Yes you read that correctly. I was highly pissed. The doors for our bedroom closets were some sliding doors with little space behind it. When we brought all of this up to the lady the next day she swore and down that she didn't tell us that the apartment was on the first floor! Then she turned back around and blamed everything on someone else. I started to act a freaking fool in that place but I didn't want to embarrass my husband! lol
I try to keep an optimistic mind so I told myself to still give the place a chance. Also we didn't have a choice. We didn't have another place to go, especially with coming from out of town. In the beginning, we were like well this place isn't THAT bad. The openness of the place was nice and the natural light was nice as well. We later realized that was about the only good thing about this place. The bug problem here is RIDICULOUS! Now I am from GA so I know water bugs sometimes find their ways in. However the bugs here did a hostel take over! We had waterbugs, ants, some small red type of baby water bugs(I still don't know what they are), and some small little centipede bugs. They scare the crap out of our 4year old. We have to get the complex pest control guy to come and spray about every two weeks. No lie.
So let's move on to the closet doors. They are constantly coming off of the tracks. Especially the ones in the master bedroom. The ones in there is all glass. The track that they were on was wobbly and crappy. The wheels kept popping off which made it hard to slide that heavy a** glass. We had to call for maintenance to come replace the wheels on NUMEROUS occasions! I honestly lost count. So the last time one of the wheels came off we didn't even report it for a while. SMH
Now mind you i said the track was off and flimsy. So the glass doors was always about to fall. ANd yes I told them about that as well. Well 3 1/2 weeks ago one of the DID fall. And that big heavy ish almost feel on our daughter. It missed her by maybe a centimeter. No exaggeration. It scared the crap out of me and her. Glass was everywhere! My husband and I had to take it out and clean all of that mess up. It took us a couple of days to get it all up. How do I know it was still there? Because I got glass stuck in my foot twice after vacuuming  about 3x's.  The day after the mirror fell, I went to the office to ask them to send maintenance to come and get the other 2 out because I didn't want the same thing to happen again. I have went over my word limit, so im about to do a part 2!
